cards.text: Last book of the Bible, friend, and it starts by telling you exactly what it is: the revelation of Jesus Christ. God gave it to Jesus to show His servants what must soon come to pass. Then it gets passed down the line to His servant John, like Minty passing a note down my old kitchen counter.

cards.question: The revelation is headed for God's servant John. Who is sent to make it known to him?
True or false: John only testifies to some of what he saw.

cards.text: Before the story even STARTS, John hands out a blessing. No sign-up sheet, no waiting list, no take-a-number machine.

cards.question: True or false: John's blessing is only for the one who reads the prophecy aloud.

cards.text: John says the time is near, and no, I'm not guessing a date, because Jesus said only the Father knows the day or hour (Matthew 24:36). My job is simple, friend: keep the ovens HOT.
Then John writes like it's a letter, addressed to churches in the province of Asia. One letter for a whole stack of churches, while I need twenty minutes to label ONE cookie box.

cards.question: John writes to the ___ churches in the province of Asia.
John sends grace and peace from Him who is and was and is to come, and from the seven spirits before His throne. Who else is it from?

cards.text: And John doesn't just say His name, he stacks up the titles: the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead, the ruler of the kings of the earth. That's not a name tag, friend, that's a BILLBOARD.

cards.question: John praises the One who loves us and has released us from our ___ by His blood.
What does John say Jesus has made His people to be?

answers.text: A kingdom and priests to God
An army and judges for God
A city and guards for God

cards.text: John gives Him the glory and power forever and ever, Amen. And then the big announcement: He is coming with the clouds.

cards.question: True or false: When He comes with the clouds, only a few people will see Him.
Every eye will see Him when He comes. John names one group in particular. Who?

answers.text: Those who crossed the Red Sea

cards.text: All the tribes of the earth will mourn because of Him, and John says so shall it be. Then a different voice speaks up, and it is NOT John's.

cards.question: This new voice says it is the Alpha and the Omega. Who is speaking?

cards.text: Now John tells it himself, and he calls himself their brother and partner in the tribulation and kingdom and perseverance that are in Jesus. Translation: John is NOT writing this from a beach chair.

cards.question: Where is John when all this happens?
True or false: John says he is on Patmos because of the word of God and his testimony about Jesus.

cards.text: On the Lord's day John is in the Spirit, and then BEHIND him comes a loud voice like a trumpet. Friend, when my oven timer dings behind me, I jump so high my gold base earns frequent flyer miles.

cards.question: What does the voice like a trumpet tell John to do?

answers.text: Write what he sees and send it
Go home and preach what he hears
Wait in silence for seven days

cards.text: It's going to seven churches, named one by one: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea. Then John turns to see the voice that was speaking with him.

cards.question: Having turned around, John sees seven golden ___.

cards.text: And among the lampstands is One like the Son of Man, dressed in a long robe with a golden sash around His chest. Hang on, friend, because John is about to use every comparison he's got.
His hair is white like wool, as white as snow, and His eyes are like a blazing fire. I've stared into a LOT of hot ovens, friend, and I don't think even I could hold that gaze.
His feet are like polished bronze refined in a furnace, and His voice is like the roar of many waters. Friend, NOBODY is interrupting that voice on a conference call.
In His right hand He holds seven stars, and a sharp double-edged sword comes from His mouth. Seven STARS in ONE hand, friend, and I need my whole mustache just to carry one tray of cookies.

cards.question: John says His face was like the ___ shining at its brightest.
John has just seen all of this up close. What does John do?

answers.text: Falls at His feet like a dead man
Covers his face and turns away
Grabs a scroll and starts writing

cards.text: Then He places His right hand on John and says, “Do not be afraid.” He calls Himself the First and the Last, which sounds a lot like the Alpha and the Omega back in verse 8.

cards.question: He calls Himself the Living One. He says He was ___, and now He is alive forever and ever.
The mystery key I shared a drawer with spent YEARS wondering what door it opened. No mystery here. What does He say He holds the keys of?
True or false: He tells John to write down only the things that will happen after this.
Then He explains the mystery of the seven stars in His right hand. What are they?

answers.text: The angels of the seven churches
The seven spirits before His throne
The seven eyes of the LORD

cards.question: True or false: The seven golden lampstands are the seven churches.

cards.text: That's where we'll pause, friend, and trust me, John's scroll is about to get a whole lot longer.

findings.problem: Too many of this stop's ten choices depend on luck or prior knowledge rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Cards 2, 3, 5, 8, 11, 12 and 14 ask for the angel, the extent of John's testimony, the scope of the blessing, the number of churches, sins, a kingdom and priests, or how many people will see Him without providing a basis for inferring those answers. These are not merely a few discovery questions among mostly informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The fill-in-the-blank questions at stop 1 card 8, stop 1 card 11 and stop 2 card 7 use blanks for seven, sins and lampstands when the preceding cards provide no way to reason out those details. They test unrevealed wording rather than meaning the baker can infer.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Many choice questions rely on antecedents or context absent from the question itself: stop 1 cards 14 and 15 use He and Him without naming Jesus, and card 17 refers to this new voice; stop 2 card 2 refers to all this, card 12 uses His with John as the nearest named person, card 13 refers to all of this, and cards 15 through 18 repeatedly use He or His without identifying the speaker. The baker has to reconstruct the subject from cards that are no longer visible.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Two important parts of the passage are only approached through negation and are never actually taught. Stop 1 card 5 can be answered false without the baker learning that verse 3 also blesses those who hear and obey. Stop 2 card 17 can be answered false without presenting verse 19's three-part command; in particular, the things that are never appear on any card.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
